baselines.name: Random
baselines.definition: Score/decision drawn uniformly at random, independent of input features.
baselines.scientific_justification: The floor: any real mechanism must exceed random to claim any signal at all. Without it, an AUROC of 0.6 has no interpretable reference point.

baselines.name: Always Answer
baselines.definition: Never abstain/review; always emit the model's raw answer.
baselines.scientific_justification: The status-quo-without-any-safety-mechanism baseline. Any abstention policy must justify its coverage loss against this baseline's correctness.

baselines.name: Always Abstain
baselines.definition: Never answer; abstain on every instance.
baselines.scientific_justification: The degenerate policy that trivially achieves zero selective risk and must be explicitly disqualified by the design principle ('always-abstain must not score as successful') — included specifically so a scoring harness that fails to check coverage is caught.

baselines.name: Generic (Non-Mechanism-Aware) Policy
baselines.definition: A single fixed confidence threshold applied identically across all three uncertainty families (arithmetic/sentiment/QA), ignoring the fact that they are non-comparable signals.
baselines.scientific_justification: Represents the naive 'one size fits all' approach the design principles explicitly forbid; demonstrating a calibrated, mechanism-aware policy beats this is the entire point of View 2's per-family requirement.

baselines.name: Calibrated, Mechanism-Aware Policy
baselines.definition: A policy with separately-fit thresholds per task family (arithmetic/sentiment/QA), calibrated only on calibration_validation.
baselines.scientific_justification: The 'best honest attempt' baseline/target — represents the ceiling of what a reasonable, non-cheating policy could achieve given each family's real discrimination ceiling (e.g. sentiment's 0.659 AUROC bounds how good any sentiment abstention policy can be).

baselines.name: Simple Statistical Predictor
baselines.definition: A single-feature logistic/threshold rule (e.g. one telemetry ratio) rather than the full trained model, fit only on development split.
baselines.scientific_justification: A trained multi-feature model must beat this simple baseline to justify its added complexity; if it does not, the added complexity is unjustified per standard ML benchmarking practice.

baselines.name: No-Memory Control
baselines.definition: Identical pipeline with FailureMemoryStore reads disabled (memory=OFF).
baselines.scientific_justification: The causal contrast that isolates memory's contribution; this is the exact ON/OFF design the Step 6 repeated-incident experiment used (retry x6 with memory OFF vs retry->retry->reconfigure->recovered with memory ON).

baselines.name: No-Retry Control
baselines.definition: Identical pipeline with RETRY disabled (arithmetic self-consistency resampling turned off).
baselines.scientific_justification: Disabling retry removed the whole observed improvement in the frozen evidence (docs/MASTER_RECORD_CONTENT.md line ~651: 'retry-off ablation') — this is the CAUSAL confound-check baseline for any claim that a downstream improvement came from retry specifically.

baselines.name: Predictor-Disabled Control
baselines.definition: Identical pipeline with the failure predictor disabled (decisions made without any prediction.score input).
baselines.scientific_justification: Isolates the predictor's causal contribution to end-to-end outcomes; the frozen evidence found little difference in one sample specifically because retry alone was already highly effective — a disclosed CONFOUND, not proof the predictor never matters (must be reported with that caveat attached every time this baseline is used).

baselines.name: Raw (Uncalibrated) Confidence
baselines.definition: The agent's own raw uncertainty signal (agreement_rate / softmax_margin / span_logit_confidence) used directly as a score, no calibration or threshold fitting.
baselines.scientific_justification: The 'no extra machinery' baseline every uncertainty benchmark task must beat to justify adding any calibration layer; also the natural pre-temperature-scaling reference point for the ECE-vs-AUROC distinction.
